security.assessment.justification.before: Why a not_affected release is not affected (the VEX/CSAF justification): an observation from a source, or (normative) an analyst's judgment citing their own words or a workspace file (security.workspace-evidence-v1). Required in practice with every not_affected status; core cannot require it.
security.assessment.justification.after: Why a not_affected release is not affected (the VEX/CSAF justification): an observation from a source, or (normative) an analyst's judgment citing their own words or a workspace file (security.file-v1). Required in practice with every not_affected status; core cannot require it.

security.assessment.component.before: The release's component that brings the vulnerability in (purl@version): which dependency an affected release needs to change. An observation is a source's word (OSV's answer for the component, or a CVE record whose packageName names it); a normative Claim is an analyst's, citing their own words or a workspace file (security.workspace-evidence-v1, via security.evidence-acquire).
security.assessment.component.after: The release's component that brings the vulnerability in (purl@version): which dependency an affected release needs to change. An observation is a source's word (OSV's answer for the component, or a CVE record whose packageName names it); a normative Claim is an analyst's, citing their own words or a workspace file (security.file-v1, via security.evidence-acquire).

security.assessment.status.before: Whether the release is affected by the vulnerability. An observation is a source's verdict (OSV, a CVE record) citing its Capture; a normative Claim is an analyst's judgment citing their own words or a workspace file (security.workspace-evidence-v1, retained by security.evidence-acquire: a source's Capture is not citable for a judgment), with their reasoning in its because. The kit's Procedures never revise a normative status; retire it to hand the assessment back to them.
security.assessment.status.after: Whether the release is affected by the vulnerability. An observation is a source's verdict (OSV, a CVE record) citing its Capture; a normative Claim is an analyst's judgment citing their own words or a workspace file (security.file-v1, retained by security.evidence-acquire: a source's Capture is not citable for a judgment), with their reasoning in its because. The kit's Procedures never revise a normative status; retire it to hand the assessment back to them.

security.audit.result.before: The auditor's judgment: exploited, not_exploited or inconclusive, citing the decisive log read (security.log-read-v1) or a workspace file (security.workspace-evidence-v1); own words are refused. Reasoning goes in a section of the incident's note. A disagreeing auditor contends (set --contend): while the slot reads conflict the answer is unknown. Never settled by a Mandate.
security.audit.result.after: The auditor's judgment: exploited, not_exploited or inconclusive, citing the decisive log read (security.file-erasable-v1) or a workspace file (security.file-v1); own words are refused. Reasoning goes in a section of the incident's note. A disagreeing auditor contends (set --contend): while the slot reads conflict the answer is unknown. Never settled by a Mandate.
